subject: Escalation: Exec sign-off requested for Medigro redlines (liability / indemnity / warranty)
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medigrohealth.com>, procurement@medigrohealth.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 14 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft redlines + commercial ask (Medigro) — need decision on exec path

Hi Elena / team,

Thanks for walking the team through the scope yesterday. Attached is our current commercial summary and the redline we received from Medigro (Medigro_redline_20250614.docx). A couple of high-level notes from our side: 

- Medigro is asking for a 20% list discount for the first 12 months and a firm 36-month warranty period for any data-loss incidents.
- They've struck out our standard one-way indemnity and replaced with broad customer-favored indemnities and removed most of our warranty limitations.
- Liability cap has been revised to unlimited for IP claims and to a €10M cap for other claims; they want to remove consequential loss carveouts.

This is a material escalation on risk. From a deal math perspective, pipeline expects $780k ARR in year one if we accept the discount, but the liability and indemnity changes are outside our standard thresholds.

Requesting guidance: please confirm whether we should route this to the exec approval path (CEO/CRO/GC) or if Legal should counter with a narrower set of concessions. My recommended compromise to present to the customer (if we escalate):
  - Liability cap: mutual cap set at €3M for the first 12 months, then re-evaluate on renewal;
  - Indemnity: mutual indemnities limited to willful misconduct and IP with express carveouts for third-party data claims where customer controls data;
  - Warranty: 12-month limited warranty language, preserve limitation of consequential damages;
  - Commercial: 10% one-time credit instead of 20% list discount (protects ARR cadence).

If Legal or Finance prefers a different posture, please advise quickly — customer is awaiting a response and plans to include the revised contract in their procurement committee agenda on Monday.

Attachments: Medigro_redline_20250614.docx; Commercial_Summary_DEAL-2025-1187.pdf

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

- Procurement insists the warranty be extended to a 36-month coverage window for critical patient-data flows (they flagged a prior vendor incident).
- They cannot accept a mutual cap; they want Redwood to carry primary responsibility for IP and security-related losses.
- The 20% discount is a hard ask tied to a delivery milestone and an expanded seat count in Year 1.

I understand these are big asks — we need a response inline with your legal/commercial norms ASAP. The procurement committee meets Monday morning CET; if we don’t have a signed position they'll escalate to their legal.

Best,

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 14 Jun 2025 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Draft redlines + commercial ask (Medigro) — need exec review

Marissa / Ben / Laura — forwarding the redlines and Elena's note. This one exceeds our standard risk band: unlimited IP exposure + €10M general cap request + elongated warranty.

Why I think escalation is warranted:
- The customer is strategic in EU health vertical and has references, but the legal asks materially change our exposure.
- We can protect revenue via a smaller commercial concession (one-time credit) if we preserve core risk protections.

My suggested options for sign-off path (please pick one):
A) Executive sign-off (GC + CEO) to accept a one-off adjusted liability cap of €3M, limited reciprocal indemnity for IP/security, 12-month warranty retained, 10% one-time credit.
B) Legal-led counteroffer: push back on IP and consequential carveouts, offer 10% credit and limited service credits for availability SLA breaches; escalate to exec only if customer refuses.
C) Finance approves a deeper commercial concession (20% discount) but requires insurance proof (E&O with €5M limit) and a special indemnity escrow clause.

Please advise route and any edits to the recommended terms. If we route to exec, I can loop in CEO and GC and prepare a short memo and redline summary for decision. Customer timeline: needs answer before Mon 09:00 CET.

Jonas
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Jun 2025 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Draft redlines + commercial ask (Medigro) — legal position and exec routing

Thanks for the clear summary, Jonas. I reviewed the redline and the risk delta is real. My recommended internal position to present to the executive approval committee: 

1) Liability cap: for this pilot/initial engagement we will offer a mutual cap of €2M (not €3M) — limited term of 12 months tied to the pilot. Any expansion beyond pilot requires renegotiation of cap and a signed addendum.

2) Indemnity: decline broad customer-favored indemnities. Offer mutual indemnity limited to willful misconduct and direct IP infringement. Add explicit carveouts for third-party claims arising from customer-controlled data and systems.

3) Warranty: decline 36-month warranty. Offer a 12-month warranty for code/functionality and a 24-month limited warranty for data retention guarantees tied to specific SOW items.

4) Commercial concession: instead of a recurring 20% discount, offer a one-time implementation credit equal to 10% ARR in Year 1. If customer insists on a deeper discount, require E&O insurance with a €5M aggregate limit and a security attestation certified within 30 days.

5) Approval threshold: I will endorse the position above and recommend CEO sign-off for final approval. If Finance (Laura) is comfortable with the credit impact, CEO can approve this one-off exception. Any request to increase the cap above €2M must go to the board/legal committee.

Next steps: Jonas — please confirm you want me to prepare an exec memo (1 page + redline highlights) and I'll add our recommended risk language and a short list of mitigations (insurance, SOW scoping, rollback rights). If you want a slightly looser cap (€3M) I will escalate that as a 'CEO + CFO only' decision.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
VP, Legal & Risk, Redwood Inference
